title: Area and definite integrals
competency: Evaluate definite integrals with anti-derivatives and use their properties.

keywords.def: The exact area under f from a to b: the limit of the Riemann sums.
The numbers a and b in ∫ from a to b.

en.text: To evaluate ∫ from a to b of f(x) dx: find any anti-derivative F (take C = 0), then compute F(b) − F(a). Write it as [F(x)] from a to b. The Fundamental Theorem says the area function A(x) has A′(x) = f(x). Be careful with signs when substituting a negative lower limit.

am.text: ዴፊኒት ኢንቲግራልን ለማስላት ማንኛውንም ፀረ-ዴሪቫቲቭ F አግኝተን F(b) − F(a) እናሰላለን።

screens.title: Area without rectangles
screens.ask: For y = x² + 1 on [−1, 2], Riemann sums would take long. F(x) = x³/3 + x has F′ = x² + 1. What is F(2) − F(−1)?
screens.after:
F(2) = 8/3 + 2 = 14/3.
F(−1) = −1/3 − 1 = −4/3.
F(2) − F(−1) = 14/3 + 4/3 = 18/3 = 6.
This equals the exact area under y = x² + 1 on [−1, 2]: no rectangles needed.

screens.title: F(b) − F(a) for y = x² + 1
screens.ask: F(x) = x³/3 + x. Move the limits a and b.
outs: ∫ from a to b = F(b) − F(a)
screens.note: a = −1, b = 2 gives 6. Try a = b: the integral is 0. Swap a and b: the sign changes.

screens.title: Definite integral by anti-derivatives
paras: If F is any anti-derivative of f: ∫ from a to b of f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a).
a and b are the limits of integration.
Notation: [F(x)] from a to b = F(b) − F(a).
screens.note: Fundamental Theorem: the area function A(x) has A′(x) = f(x).

screens.title: Properties
paras: ∫ from a to b = ∫ from a to c + ∫ from c to b.
∫ from a to b = −∫ from b to a.
∫ kf = k ∫ f, and ∫ (f ± g) = ∫ f ± ∫ g (same limits).

screens.title: The properties with numbers
screens.ask: Tap each property. All use f(x) = 2x, F(x) = x².
items: ∫ from 0 to 3 = ∫ from 0 to 1 + ∫ from 1 to 3: 9 = 1 + 8.
∫ from 0 to 3 6x dx = 3 × ∫ from 0 to 3 2x dx = 3 × 9 = 27.

screens.ask: Evaluate the definite integral with an anti-derivative: ∫ from 1 to 3 (3x² + 2x) dx = ___
Evaluate the definite integral: ∫ from 0 to 5 (x² + 1) dx = ___
Evaluate the definite integral: ∫ from −1 to 0 (x³ − 3x + 1) dx = ___
screens.why:
F(x) = x⁴/4 − 3x²/2 + x.
F(0) = 0.
F(−1) = 1/4 − 3/2 − 1 = 1/4 − 10/4 = −9/4.
F(0) − F(−1) = 0 − (−9/4) = 9/4.
Trap: subtracting a negative makes it positive.

screens.ask: Evaluate the definite integral: ∫ from 1 to 4 (2x + 1/x²) dx = ___
Evaluate the definite integral: ∫ from −2 to 3 (−3x² + 4x − 5) dx = ___

screens.text: True or false? A power plant makes x³ kW on day x. The area under y = x³ on [0, 5] (156 1/4) is the total made in the first 5 days.
screens.why:
y = x³ is a rate (kW on each day).
The area under a rate graph is the total amount.
∫ from 0 to 5 x³ dx = [x⁴/4] = 625/4 = 156 1/4.
True.
screens.clue: What does area under a rate mean?

screens.ask: Missing upper limit: ∫ from 0 to k 3x² dx = 64. Find k = ___
screens.why:
Anti-derivative of 3x² is x³.
∫ from 0 to k 3x² dx = k³ − 0 = k³.
k³ = 64, so k = 4.
Check: 4³ = 64. ✓

test.text: Property of definite integrals: ∫ from 5 to 2 f(x) dx equals
test.why:
∫ from a to b f = F(b) − F(a).
∫ from 5 to 2 f = F(2) − F(5) = −(F(5) − F(2)).
So reversing the limits changes the sign: −∫ from 2 to 5 f(x) dx.
0 is only for equal limits, ∫ from a to a.

screens.title: ∫ 4x³ dx
steps: Divide by 4 and multiply by 4: x⁴ + C.

screens.why:
∫ 2x dx = 2 × x²/2 = x².
∫ 3 dx = 3x.
Answer: x² + 3x + C.
Check: (x² + 3x)′ = 2x + 3. ✓
